chunks: The elder jurist Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa from 'Ali b. al-Hakam from Dawud b. al-Nu'man from Sayf al-Tammar from Abu Basir. He said: Al-Sadiq Abu 'Abdillah Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said:

Indeed, the servant is in a period of respite in his affair between him and forty years of age. When he reaches forty years of age, God, Mighty and Majestic, reveals to His two angels: "Indeed, I have granted My servant a lifespan, so be harsh, be strict, and be vigilant; and record against him the small and the great of his deeds, and the minor and the major of them."

key_terms.عَمَّرْتُ: I have given a lifespan — refers to God granting the servant a full life
key_terms.فُسْحَة: Respite or expanse — a period of leniency before full accountability
key_terms.مَلَكَيْهِ: His two angels — the recording angels assigned to each person

ai.seo_question: What happens when a person reaches forty years of age according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that a person is given leniency before the age of forty, after which God commands the recording angels to be more strict and diligent in recording all deeds, both small and great. This hadith was narrated in the assembly of Shaykh al-Saduq in 367 AH and reflects the classical understanding that forty years marks a pivotal age of full accountability, echoing the Quranic concept of maturity at forty (Quran 46:15).
